newsitem.title: INDIA: India Bajaj shr drops on poor Q1 reports.
newsitem.headline: India Bajaj shr drops on poor Q1 reports.

text.p: Shares of India's largest two-wheeler maker Bajaj Auto lost 37.50 rupees, or 4.16 percent, to 864.0 at the Bombay exchange on Monday on reports of a drop in first quarter 1997/98 sales, traders said.
Bajaj Auto's turnover dropped six percent in the first quarter of 1997/98 (April-March), the Financial Express newspaper reported on Sunday.
"Negative first quarter results have dampened sentiment in the stock," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage. He however said the poor performance was largely expected.
Bajaj's first quarter production had dropped 17 percent over the period from April to June, compared to the corresponding period the previous year, the Financial Express added.
"This is the first time Bajaj Auto has lost market share and production is down," the daily said.

It quoted firm chairman Rahul Bajaj as telling shareholders at the annual general meeting that he expected a difficult year ahead, with the company having yielded 6.5 percent of its two-wheeler market share to competitors in 1996/97.
Bajaj's 52nd annual general meeting was held in the western city of Pune on Saturday.
The Bajaj Auto chief attributed the loss of market share to the cascading effect of reduced capital expenditure by the federal government, the daily said.
It quoted him as saying the firm would be unable to recoup its loss in market share this year and adding that this might not happen until 1999/2000.
